routes.description: Establish that substantive arguments can rationally clarify and support theism despite dependence on prior commitments, then defend the actuality principle against persistence counterexamples and trace contemporaneous explanatory dependence to a purely actual divine terminus.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if detailed premise-level argument remains epistemically relevant, persistence requires positive contemporaneous actualities rather than mere noninterference, the resulting explanatory regress cannot terminate in potential or composite physical reality, and its terminus qualifies as divine.

motionBridge.description: Connect the defended Aristotelian causal reasoning to both the existence of a good argument for God and identification of its ultimate actualizer as divine.

centralBridges.description: Show that audience-relative, informal, and formally reconstructed reasoning can provide rational support without needing to compel every competent opponent.
Show that persistence and change alike depend on already actual explanatory conditions, preserving the actuality principle against the chair and universe counterexamples.
Show that contemporaneous explanatory dependence cannot terminate in anything composite or retaining unactualized potentiality, and therefore requires a purely actual terminus.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require detailed examination of particular premises and inferences instead of resolving the theistic dispute solely through abstract argument theory.
Explain why a simple terminus without parts or potentiality is not an ordinary physical constituent but bears the relevant divine status.

routes.description: Establish that premise-conclusion arguments have limited power across deep theoretical disagreement, that worldviews should instead be compared globally, and that a simpler persistence account plus an ultimate physical level blocks Feser's regress to a divine actualizer.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if Feser's proof cannot rationally move the strongest naturalist without antecedently disputed premises, persistence can occur without a distinct actualizer, or the explanatory hierarchy can terminate coherently in physical simples or fundamental physical reality rather than God.

motionBridge.description: Connect the methodological and persistence objections to the conclusion that Feser's Aristotelian proof does not establish a good argument for God.

centralBridges.description: Show that arguments principally expose consequences or inconsistency because competent opponents may rationally reject premises inherited from a rival theory.
Require global comparison of rival theories by explanatory scope and economy rather than treating a formally valid reconstruction as independently dispute-settling.
Show that successive universal states or coordinated persisting properties can be realized without a distinct already actual actualizer.
Show that constitution may bottom out in physical simples, a quantum field, or another fundamental physical level without further explanation or divinity.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Assess philosophical merit against the strongest informed rival theory rather than against sympathetic, unprepared, or already premise-accepting audiences.
Establish that the noninterference account of persistence is a genuine and comparatively simpler alternative theory rather than a verbal restatement of actualization.

sections.rationale: This issue determines what counts as a good argument, whether premise rejection limits rational force, and whether audience-relative usefulness, informal support, or formal reconstruction remains epistemically significant.

sections.title: Particular Arguments and Global Theory Comparison
sections.rationale: This issue structures whether the debate should turn on detailed scrutiny of individual proofs and disputed premises or on comparative virtues of the complete theistic and naturalistic theories.

sections.title: Actualization, Persistence, and Noninterference
sections.rationale: This is the principal direct clash over whether unchanged properties and successive states require an already actual actualizer, and therefore whether the foundational premise of the Aristotelian proof survives.

sections.title: Microstructure and Contemporaneous Explanatory Dependence
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether persisting chemical and physical structure positively explains macroscopic persistence or merely forms a coordinated state that continues without any distinct actual cause.

sections.title: Ultimate Physical Level or Purely Actual Terminus
sections.rationale: This issue governs the proof's final inference: whether explanatory descent may stop with physical simples or fundamental fields, or whether any genuine terminus must lack composition and potentiality and thus be divine.

routes.description: Establish that human beings possess a limited but genuine volitional capacity to regulate conscious attention, activate reason, and thereby influence deliberation and action without claiming unrestricted control over mental content, circumstances, or outcomes.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if regulating awareness is directly supportable as an agent-caused, non-necessitated capacity that changes deliberative engagement and cannot be exhaustively redescribed as compelled inference, strongest-desire operation, randomness, or mechanical event causation.

motionBridge.description: Show that voluntary regulation of conscious focus and rational engagement constitutes free will under the motion's volitional-capacity alternative.

centralBridges.description: Precisely distinguish choosing the degree and method of conscious engagement from choosing every thought, desire, conclusion, action, or outcome.
Explain how a person can cause a choice to focus without that choice being necessitated by prior events or reduced to a causeless random occurrence.
Ground the claimed capacity in awareness of modulating attention, including the ability to sustain focus, broaden context, or evade recognized considerations.
Connect chosen cognitive engagement to changes in deliberation, value ordering, operative desires, and consequent conduct.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Support a conception of consciousness and causation broad enough to permit volitional agency rather than assuming an exclusively mechanical model.
Account for coercion, bodily processes, unchosen emotions, and environmental limits while preserving the narrower claimed control over awareness.

routes.description: Deny both ultimate control and the proposed capacity to activate reason by showing that actions, attention, desires, and convictions arise through determining influences or indeterminacy, neither of which makes the person the controlling author.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the proposed act of focusing remains unexplained outside determination or randomness, while introspection, deliberation, evasion, regret, and coercive choice can be accounted for without an independent volitional power.

motionBridge.description: Show that neither ultimate authorship nor voluntary control of rational focus survives the alternatives of causal determination and indeterminacy.

centralBridges.description: Apply the determined-or-random dilemma to actions and mental events, including the purported agent-caused decision to activate awareness.
Explain attention, arising considerations, rational conviction, and action through unchosen influences rather than proactive selection by a chooser.
Account for conduct, evasion, self-modification, and value-sensitive deliberation through first-order and higher-order desires whose operative strength is not freely chosen.
Establish that an immediate experience of agency does not by itself settle whether the apparent control is genuine or instead admits an alternative explanation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test libertarian control by asking what could explain divergent choices under otherwise identical relevant conditions.
Keep the conceptual objection applicable whether consciousness is characterized as material, immaterial, or emergent.

sections.rationale: Accounts of mind, coercion, bodily limits, emotion formation, regret, and evasion test whether the competing causal models remain coherent when applied beyond abstract choice examples.

routes.description: Establish that religion, assessed as a broad historical and contemporary social force, produces a net balance of human flourishing through moral motivation, service, solidarity, reform, reconciliation, and meaning that outweighs harms committed in its name.
routes.successCriteria: The pro route succeeds by showing a material causal contribution from religion to durable benefits, explaining why religious harms are neither universal nor uniquely religious, and defending those benefits against claims that they are fully replaceable by secular alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Connect religion's beneficial and harmful effects to an on-balance judgment under a consistent causal standard and comparative baseline.

centralBridges.description: Show that religious belief and organization motivate material care, durable community, interfaith cooperation, and institutions that advance human welfare.
Show that religious commitments can motivate moral reform, forgiveness, peacebuilding, and reconciliation across communal divisions.
Distinguish authentic faith from fanaticism and identify political, ethnic, or ideological causes that prevent religious wrongdoing from defining religion as a whole.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how higher purpose, humility, binding obligation, hope, and self-transcendence can direct believers toward better conduct.
Explain how religious participation can coexist with democratic authority, equal liberty, interpretation, and noncoercive engagement.

routes.description: Establish that religion is not a force for good overall because supernatural authority, exclusive truth claims, and religious institutions recurrently amplify conflict, credulity, coercion, repression, and resistance to correction, while genuine benefits remain available without religion.
routes.successCriteria: The con route succeeds by tracing substantial harms to religion's distinctive doctrines or authority structures, rebutting attempts to externalize those harms, and showing that charity, solidarity, transcendence, and moral conduct do not require supernatural belief.

motionBridge.description: Show under an even-handed causal and counterfactual test that attributable harms outweigh religiously distinctive benefits or defeat the claimed net good.

centralBridges.description: Show how divine warrant, exclusive truth, and sacred identity intensify conflict, harden political disputes, and legitimize coercion or violence.
Show how unaccountable authority and insulation from evidence enable cruelty, discrimination, sexual repression, public-health obstruction, and lost freedom.
Show that charity, solidarity, courage, consolation, transcendence, and reform can arise through secular humanism and therefore do not uniquely vindicate religion.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify where religion supplies motives, permissions, identities, institutions, or escalation mechanisms rather than merely accompanying independent conflict.
Explain how church-state separation, individual autonomy, evidence-based inquiry, and nonreligious community furnish a less coercive alternative.

sections.rationale: This issue tests the rival accounts of how perceivers encounter structure, whether mind dependence supports theism, and whether evolutionary and scientific explanation can accommodate the observed relation between cognition and world.

sections.title: Genesis, Symbolic Truth, and Historical Reference
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether Genesis supplies truth-bearing purposive orientation and disciplined reference to reality, or whether its analogical value can be retained without accepting privileged divine or historical claims.

sections.title: Resurrection, Personal Identity, and Pattern Persistence
sections.rationale: This issue bears directly on whether continuity of identity beyond changing matter makes bodily resurrection coherent and religiously necessary, or whether pragmatic insight and structural abstraction leave the historical claim unsupported.

sections.title: Worship, Value Hierarchies, and Social Meaning
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether worship and sacred centers enact genuinely transcendent purposes that organize communal life, or whether moral formation, cohesion, and collective action admit bottom-up social explanations without implying supernatural truth.
